definition: Moses for Mere Mortals (MMM) is a free open source software composed of a set of scripts designed to allow the automation of processes for the installation and operation of the Moses Open Source Translation System, a statistical machine translation system.
details: MMM builds a translation chain prototype with Moses + IRSTLM + RandLM + MGIZA. The first version of Moses for Mere Mortals was published in November 2009, and it has been updated and tested on Linux - Ubuntu distributions. MMM is available in the GitHub Project Hosting website.

explainer.lead: Moses for Mere Mortals (MMM) is free open-source software: a set of scripts that automates installing and operating the Moses statistical machine translation system. It lowers the setup barrier for building translation prototypes.

tiers.eli5: It is a bundle of helper scripts that sets up a translation toolkit for you so you do not have to do it by hand.
tiers.practitioner: It builds a translation chain prototype with Moses plus IRSTLM, RandLM, and MGIZA. It has been updated and tested on Linux Ubuntu distributions, so other environments are a known limitation.
tiers.paperLevel: A script collection automating installation and operation of the Moses statistical machine translation system with Moses, IRSTLM, RandLM, and MGIZA; first published November 2009, tested on Ubuntu Linux.

explainer.example: A user runs the MMM scripts on Ubuntu to assemble a working Moses plus IRSTLM pipeline for a translation prototype.
